name: Salif Keita
milestone_by_age_26: Became lead singer of the government-sponsored Rail Band of Bamako (~1970-71) and then Les Ambassadeurs du Motel de Bamako (1973), one of Mali's most popular bands, all before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born to the Keita royal family in Djoliba but raised in a poor farming household and ostracized for his albinism, Keita moved to Bamako at age 18 and began singing on the streets and in nightclubs. Within a few years he was discovered by Tidiane Kone and joined the government-sponsored Rail Band, becoming its star vocalist before departing for Les Ambassadeurs in 1973.
family_context_summary: Born into the Keita royal family tracing lineage to Sundiata Keita, founder of the Mali Empire, but raised in a poor farming household and cast out for his albinism and choice to pursue music.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family rejected his musical ambitions as it violated noble occupational prohibitions; no domain advantage transferred.
primary_early_advantage_tags: albinism ostracism, poverty, royal lineage rejection, government band pipeline, vocal talent
evidence_summary: Keita was born into royal lineage but grew up poor and was ostracized for his albinism, creating intense adversity that catalyzed his musical career. He moved to Bamako at 18 and sang on the streets before being discovered by Tidiane Kone and joining the government-sponsored Rail Band around 1970-71. By 1973 he had joined Les Ambassadeurs, and by age 26 he was the lead singer of one of Mali's most popular bands. His spectacular vocal talent was noted from the start, but his path was driven by adversity rather than family advantage.
starting_point: Born to the Keita royal family in Djoliba, Mali, but raised in a poor farming household and ostracized by family and community for his albinism.
current_position: Retired from recording in 2018 but returned with acoustic album So Kono in 2025; known as the Golden Voice of Africa; resides in Mali.

trajectory.event: Left Djoliba for Bamako and began performing as a street musician and in nightclubs.
Joined the government-sponsored Rail Band of Bamako as its star vocalist.
Left the Rail Band to join rival group Les Ambassadeurs du Motel de Bamako.
Received the National Order of Guinea from President Sekou Toure and composed the praise song Mandjou.
Moved to Paris and launched a solo career.
Released Soro, a landmark Afropop album that set a new standard for electric African music.
Grammy nomination for the album Amen, a collaboration with Joe Zawinul.
Announced retirement from recording.

name: Thierry Henry
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1998 FIFA World Cup with France at age 21, was named Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year at 19, won the Ligue 1 title with Monaco at 20, and won Euro 2000 at 23.
early_history_summary: Henry grew up in the Paris suburb of Les Ulis and joined local club CO Les Ulis at age 7. At 13 he was recruited to the elite Clairefontaine academy and signed for Monaco, making his professional debut at 17 under Arsene Wenger. He was named Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year in 1996 and won the World Cup with France in 1998.
family_context_summary: Born to a working-class family in Les Ulis, a suburb of Paris; father Antoine is from Guadeloupe and mother Maryse is from Martinique. Father pushed him to attend football training from a young age.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was not a football professional but pressured Henry to attend training and was involved in his early football development; no professional domain expertise transferred.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Clairefontaine academy, Arsene Wenger mentorship, physical prodigy, French football system, Monaco
evidence_summary: Henry grew up in a working-class Paris suburb but was identified as a football prodigy early, scoring all six goals in a match at 13 that led to recruitment by Monaco and admission to the elite Clairefontaine academy. Arsene Wenger provided sustained mentorship from youth through professional debut at 17. By 21, Henry was a World Cup winner. His father pushed him toward football but had no professional domain expertise. The French elite academy pipeline and Wenger's mentorship were the dominant early advantages.
starting_point: Born to a working-class family in Les Ulis, a suburb of Paris; father from Guadeloupe and mother from Martinique; father pushed him into football from a young age.
current_position: Football manager and media pundit; former Arsenal and France legend; all-time Arsenal top scorer with 228 goals; estimated net worth approximately $130 million; resides in London.

trajectory.event: Made professional debut for Monaco under Arsene Wenger.
Named Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year and won Ligue 1 title with Monaco.
Won the FIFA World Cup with France, scoring three goals in the tournament.
Signed for Arsenal for 11 million pounds, reuniting with Arsene Wenger.
Led Arsenal to an unbeaten Premier League season, scoring 30 goals.
Won the historic treble with Barcelona including the Champions League.
Retired from professional football after stint at New York Red Bulls.
Managed France U21 and Olympic football team at the Paris Olympics.

name: Helena Suková
milestone_by_age_26: Reached the 1984 Australian Open singles final at age 19 (ending Navratilova's 74-match winning streak), won first WTA singles title at 16, and won the 1985 US Open doubles title at 20.
early_history_summary: Born into one of Czechoslovakia's most prominent tennis families, Suková started playing at the Sparta Prague club as a child with her mother as coach. She won her first tournament at age 10, turned professional in 1981, won her first WTA singles title in January 1982 at 16, and made her Grand Slam breakthrough at the 1984 Australian Open.
family_context_summary: Born into a prominent Czech tennis family in Prague; mother Vera Sukova was a Wimbledon singles finalist in 1962 and a devoted coach; father Cyril Suk II was president of the Czechoslovak Tennis Federation.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was a Wimbledon finalist and one of the best tennis coaches in the world, providing sustained individualized coaching from the beginning. Father was president of the Czechoslovak Tennis Federation, providing institutional access.
primary_early_advantage_tags: tennis family, mother as coach, Wimbledon finalist mother, federation president father, Sparta Prague club, Czech tennis tradition
evidence_summary: Suková was born into one of the most influential Czech tennis families: her mother was a Wimbledon finalist and devoted coach, and her father was president of the Czechoslovak Tennis Federation. She grew up at the Sparta Prague club, started tournaments at 10, and received sustained coaching from her mother from the beginning. By 16 she won her first WTA title, and at 19 she ended Navratilova's 74-match winning streak to reach the Australian Open final. The family-domain apprenticeship was the dominant early advantage, supplemented by the elite Czech tennis pipeline.
starting_point: Born into a prominent Czech tennis family in Prague; mother was a Wimbledon singles finalist and father was president of the Czechoslovak Tennis Federation.
current_position: Retired from professional tennis since 1998; inducted into International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2018; resides in Prague, Czech Republic.

trajectory.event: Won her first WTA singles title at the Newport News tournament in Virginia.
Reached Australian Open singles final, ending Navratilova's 74-match winning streak in the semifinal.
Won US Open women's doubles title with partner Claudia Kohde-Kilsch.
Won Wimbledon women's doubles title and defeated both Navratilova and Evert at Eastbourne.
Achieved world No. 1 ranking in women's doubles.
Won Wimbledon mixed doubles title with her brother Cyril Suk.
Retired from the professional tennis tour.
Inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

name: Bertrand Piccard
milestone_by_age_26: Became a European pioneer of hang gliding and microlight flying during the 1970s, winning his first hang gliding competition at age 17 in 1975, establishing himself in the sport before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born into a dynasty of explorers and scientists, Piccard took up hang gliding at age 16 in 1974 despite an initial fear of heights. He won his first competition the following year and became one of the European pioneers of the sport, developing skills in concentration and risk management that would later underpin his exploration career.
family_context_summary: Born into a family of explorers and scientists in Lausanne, Switzerland; grandfather Auguste Piccard invented the pressurized cockpit and stratospheric balloon; father Jacques Piccard made the world's deepest ocean dive.
parent_family_domain_summary: Grandfather and father were world-renowned explorers and scientists, providing deep domain immersion in exploration, aviation, and extreme environments from childhood.
primary_early_advantage_tags: explorer dynasty, grandfather stratospheric balloon, father deep sea dive, Swiss Alps hang gliding frontier, overcoming fear of heights
evidence_summary: Piccard was born into a legendary family of explorers: his grandfather invented the stratospheric balloon and his father made the world's deepest ocean dive. This provided deep domain immersion in exploration and extreme environments. He took up hang gliding at 16 in the Swiss Alps, won his first competition at 17, and became a European pioneer of the sport. His family name and connections provided access and inspiration, though his specific hang gliding achievements were self-driven. The family-domain apprenticeship in exploration was the dominant early advantage.
starting_point: Born in Lausanne, Switzerland into a dynasty of explorers and scientists; grandfather Auguste invented the stratospheric balloon and father Jacques made the world's deepest ocean dive.
current_position: Founder and chairman of the Solar Impulse Foundation; psychiatrist, explorer, and environmentalist; resides in Switzerland.

trajectory.event: First hang glider flight in the Swiss Alps, overcoming a fear of heights.
Won his first hang gliding competition.
Became European hang-glider aerobatics champion.
Won the first Transatlantic Balloon Race with Wim Verstraeten.
Completed the first non-stop round-the-world balloon flight in Breitling Orbiter 3.
Launched the Solar Impulse project with Andre Borschberg.
Completed the first round-the-world solar-powered flight with Solar Impulse.

name: Norman Foster, Baron Foster of Thames Bank
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Henry Fellowship to the Yale School of Architecture in 1961 after graduating from the University of Manchester, having also won a RIBA silver medal in 1959 for architectural drawing.
early_history_summary: Born into a working-class family in Stockport, Foster left school at 16 and worked in the City Treasurer's office before National Service in the RAF. He worked at an architectural firm, then studied architecture at Manchester University while working multiple jobs to fund his studies. His talent was recognized with a RIBA silver medal in 1959 and the prestigious Henry Fellowship to Yale in 1961.
family_context_summary: Born to a working-class family in Reddish, Stockport; father was a machine painter at Metropolitan-Vickers works and mother worked in a bakery; the family lived in poverty in Manchester.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father's work as a machine painter at an engineering works influenced Foster toward engineering and design, but no professional architectural domain expertise was transferred.
primary_early_advantage_tags: working-class poverty, self-funded education, RIBA silver medal, Yale fellowship, left school at 16, multiple jobs
evidence_summary: Foster grew up in poverty in a working-class Manchester family, left school at 16, and entirely self-funded his architecture education through jobs as an ice-cream salesman, bouncer, and bakery worker. His talent was recognized with a RIBA silver medal in 1959 and the Henry Fellowship to Yale in 1961. At Yale he met Richard Rogers, with whom he later co-founded Team 4. His path was driven by self-creation against economic constraints, with the Yale fellowship providing the key institutional breakthrough at age 26.
starting_point: Born to a working-class family in Reddish, Stockport; father was a machine painter at Metropolitan-Vickers and mother worked in a bakery; the family lived in poverty in Manchester.
current_position: Founder and executive chairman of Foster + Partners, the largest architectural practice in the UK; Pritzker Prize laureate; life peer; resides in Switzerland.

trajectory.event: Won RIBA silver medal and 105 pounds for a measured drawing of Bourn Windmill.
Graduated from Manchester and won the Henry Fellowship to Yale School of Architecture.
Co-founded architectural practice Team 4 with Richard Rogers, Wendy Cheesman, and Su Brumwell.
Established Foster Associates, later rebranded as Foster + Partners.
Awarded a life peerage as Baron Foster of Thames Bank.
Won the Pritzker Architecture Prize, the field's highest honor.

name: Serge Klarsfeld
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Klarsfeld met his wife Beate in 1960 and the Eichmann trial in 1961 solidified their commitment, but their Nazi-hunting activism began in the mid-to-late 1960s with the first major exploit in 1968 when Beate slapped German Chancellor Kiesinger.
early_history_summary: Born in Bucharest in 1935, Klarsfeld's father was killed at Auschwitz in 1943 when Serge was 8. He studied at the Sorbonne and the Institute of Political Science of Paris, and met his future wife Beate Kunzel in 1960. Their activism began in earnest after the Eichmann trial but their first major public action came in 1968.
family_context_summary: Born in Bucharest, Romania to a Jewish family; father was arrested by the Gestapo in Nice in 1943 and killed at Auschwitz; Serge, his mother, and sister survived in hiding.
evidence_summary: Klarsfeld was born in Bucharest in 1935 and survived the Holocaust as a child in hiding in Nice, though his father was killed at Auschwitz. He studied at the Sorbonne and Institute of Political Science of Paris, and met his wife Beate in 1960. By age 26 (1961), he had not yet achieved a material milestone in activism; his Nazi-hunting career began in the mid-to-late 1960s with the first major public action in 1968.

name: Fyodor Konyukhov
milestone_by_age_26: Completed his first solo expedition at age 15 (1966) crossing the Sea of Azov, and undertook his first major scientific sailing expedition in 1977 (age 25) retracing Vitus Bering's voyage across 4,000 nautical miles.
early_history_summary: Born in a fishing village on the Sea of Azov, Konyukhov's father and grandfather were fishermen who inspired his love of exploration. He undertook his first solo expedition at 15, crossing the Sea of Azov in a stolen fishing boat after his father broke his homemade vessel. He attended nautical school in Odessa and served in the Soviet Navy before launching his first major scientific expedition in 1977.
family_context_summary: Born in the village of Chkalovo in the Ukrainian SSR; father Philip was a fisherman on the Sea of Azov who took his son on fishing trips; grandfather Mikhail was also a fisherman who knew polar explorer Georgy Sedov.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father and grandfather were fishermen who provided direct immersion in maritime life and seafaring from childhood; grandfather's connection to polar explorer Georgy Sedov inspired Konyukhov's exploration ambitions.
primary_early_advantage_tags: fishing family, Sea of Azov, grandfather explorer connection, nautical school, first expedition at 15, Soviet Navy
evidence_summary: Konyukhov grew up in a fishing village on the Sea of Azov, where his father and grandfather were fishermen who provided direct maritime immersion from childhood. His grandfather's stories of polar explorer Georgy Sedov inspired his exploration ambitions. At 15, he undertook his first solo expedition crossing the Sea of Azov, and by 25 he completed a major scientific sailing expedition. His path was driven by early domain immersion and self-created repetition in maritime exploration, with his father's opposition (breaking his homemade boat) serving as a constraint that catalyzed his determination.
starting_point: Born in the village of Chkalovo, Ukrainian SSR; father was a fisherman on the Sea of Azov and grandfather was also a fisherman who knew polar explorer Georgy Sedov.
current_position: Russian Orthodox priest, explorer, artist, and author; continues expedition work; resides in Russia.

trajectory.event: Completed first solo expedition crossing the Sea of Azov in a stolen fishing boat.
Undertook first major scientific sailing expedition retracing Vitus Bering's voyage across 4,000 nautical miles.
Reached the North Pole as part of the Russian autonomous expedition Arktika.
Made the first solo skiing trip to the North Pole in Russian history.
Completed the Seven Summits, climbing the highest peak on each continent.
Ordained as an Eastern Orthodox priest in the Ukrainian Orthodox Church.
Completed a solo balloon circumnavigation of the world in 11 days.

name: Mustafa Dağıstanlı
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1954 World Championship in freestyle wrestling at age 23, the 1956 Olympic gold medal at 25, and the 1957 World Championship at 26, establishing himself as one of the best wrestlers in the world.
early_history_summary: Born in a village in Carsamba, Turkey, Dağıstanlı grew up with Turkish oil wrestling before taking up formal wrestling at 18 while serving in the Turkish Naval Forces. He won his first national championship in 1951 at age 20 by defeating the 1948 Olympic champion, and became World Champion in 1954 in his first international championship.
family_context_summary: Born in 1931 in Soguroinar village of Carsamba, Turkey; family background not extensively documented beyond village origins.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family wrestling background transferred.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Turkish oil wrestling culture, naval forces wrestling, national team, defeated Olympic champion, wrestling tradition
evidence_summary: Dağıstanlı grew up in a Turkish village immersed in the country's deep wrestling culture, practicing oil wrestling from a young age before taking up formal freestyle wrestling at 18 in the Turkish Naval Forces. He won his first national championship at 20 by defeating the 1948 Olympic champion, became World Champion at 23 in his first international championship, and won Olympic gold at 25. The Turkish wrestling tradition and institutional pipeline through the naval forces and national team were the dominant early advantages, supplemented by his natural physical talent.
starting_point: Born in 1931 in Soguroinar village of Carsamba, Turkey; grew up in a rural village immersed in Turkish wrestling culture.
current_position: Died on September 18, 2022 at age 91; final role: retired wrestler and coach, former member of the Turkish Grand National Assembly from 1973 to 1980.

name: Greta Thunberg
milestone_by_age_26: Started the School Strike for Climate in August 2018 at age 15, inspiring the global Fridays for Future movement; named Time Person of the Year in 2019 at 16; delivered landmark speech at the UN Climate Action Summit in 2019.
early_history_summary: Born in Stockholm to opera singer Malena Ernman and actor Svante Thunberg, Greta first learned about climate change at age 8 and became deeply depressed, eventually diagnosed with Asperger syndrome, OCD, and selective mutism. In May 2018 she won a writing competition about the environment, and in August 2018 she began her solo school strike outside the Swedish parliament, which quickly went viral and inspired millions globally.
family_context_summary: Born in Stockholm to opera singer Malena Ernman and actor Svante Thunberg; paternal grandfather was actor and director Olof Thunberg; comfortable middle-class family with significant media and public profile.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother is a well-known opera singer and climate activist; father is an actor; family had media connections and public profile that may have facilitated early attention, though parents initially did not support the school strike.
primary_early_advantage_tags: social media virality, family media profile, Asperger's focus, climate crisis urgency, Swedish progressive context, solo strike
evidence_summary: Thunberg was born into a comfortable Stockholm family with famous parents in the arts, providing media connections that may have facilitated early attention. Her Asperger's, OCD, and selective mutism created intense focus on climate change from age 8, catalyzing her activism. The school strike in August 2018 went viral through social media, and the global climate movement provided a structural wave. Her family's media profile and the social media platform were the key distribution mechanisms, while her neurodivergent intensity was the catalyst. Parents initially opposed her strike but came to support it.
starting_point: Born in Stockholm, Sweden to opera singer Malena Ernman and actor Svante Thunberg; comfortable middle-class family with significant media and public profile.
current_position: Climate activist and author; graduated from high school in 2023; continues climate advocacy and public speaking; resides in Sweden.

trajectory.event: Started solo School Strike for Climate outside the Swedish parliament in August.
Named Time magazine's Person of the Year, the youngest ever; delivered landmark speech at UN Climate Action Summit.

Nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize for the second consecutive year.
Graduated from high school and ended her school climate strikes.
Continued climate activism and political engagement, including protests against fossil fuel subsidies.

name: Danny Makkelie
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Eredivisie debut in the 2009-10 season at age 26, reaching the top tier of Dutch professional football refereeing, having refereed his first professional match at 22.
early_history_summary: Born in Curaçao to a Dutch Royal Marine father, Makkelie moved to the Netherlands as a young boy. He began refereeing football and basketball at age 10 and was refereeing adult matches as a teenager. He was invited into the KNVB refereeing system and refereed his first professional match at 22 before making his Eredivisie debut at 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Willemstad, Curaçao to a Dutch Royal Marine father; family returned to the Netherlands when Makkelie was young; father was supportive and drove him to matches.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a Dutch Royal Marine who encouraged and supported his refereeing path, driving him to matches, but had no professional refereeing domain expertise.

His father, a Royal Marine, was his biggest supporter and drove him to matches. He was invited into the KNVB refereeing system and refereed his first professional match at 22, making his Eredivisie debut at 26. His path was driven by self-created domain repetition from an exceptionally young age, with the KNVB pipeline providing institutional structure.

current_position: UEFA elite category referee and part-time police inspector in Rotterdam; selected to referee at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

name: Alfonso Cuarón
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Cuarón's first feature film Solo con tu pareja was released in 1991 when he was 30; by age 26 he was working as a technician in Mexican television after being expelled from film school.
early_history_summary: Born in Mexico City to a doctor and a pharmaceutical biochemist, Cuarón began making films with a Super 8 camera as a child. He studied philosophy at UNAM and film at CUEC but was expelled before graduating. He then worked as a technician in Mexican television and took on various gigs to hone his technical skills, eventually becoming an assistant director before his first feature film at 30.
family_context_summary: Born in Mexico City to Alfredo Cuarón, a doctor specializing in nuclear medicine, and Cristina Orozco, a pharmaceutical biochemist; comfortable middle-class upbringing until parents separated in the early 1970s.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were professionals in medicine and biochemistry, not in film or the arts; no direct domain expertise transferred, though middle-class background supported early creative exploration.
evidence_summary: Cuarón was born into a comfortable middle-class family in Mexico City and began making films with a Super 8 camera as a child. He studied film at CUEC but was expelled, then worked as a technician in Mexican television. By age 26 (November 1987), he had not yet achieved a material milestone; he was working in television and taking on various gigs. His first feature film, Solo con tu pareja, came in 1991 at age 30, and his breakthrough with Y tu mama tambien came in 2001 at age 40.

name: Bjarne Riis
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first professional victory at stage 9 of the 1989 Giro d'Italia at age 25, riding as a support rider for Laurent Fignon, and helped Fignon win the 1989 Giro d'Italia overall.
early_history_summary: Born in Herning, Denmark, Riis began cycling at local club Herning CK. When he was not selected for the 1984 Olympics, former cyclist Kim Andersen advised him to start his professional career in Luxembourg. His professional career started in 1986 with modest results, but after joining Laurent Fignon's Systeme U team in 1989, he won his first professional stage at the Giro d'Italia.
family_context_summary: Born in Herning, Denmark; began cycling at local club Herning CK; family background not extensively documented beyond modest Danish origins.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family cycling domain expertise transferred.

evidence_summary: Riis grew up in Herning, Denmark, and began cycling at the local club Herning CK. After being passed over for the 1984 Olympics, former cyclist Kim Andersen advised him to turn professional in Luxembourg rather than Italy. His early professional years were difficult with no personal wins, but his career was transformed when Laurent Fignon recruited him to Systeme U in 1989, where he won his first professional stage at the Giro d'Italia. Fignon's mentorship and the elite team structure were the key accelerants, while the early adversity of a tough apprenticeship with low pay built resilience.
starting_point: Born in Herning, Denmark; began cycling at local club Herning CK; modest Danish background.
current_position: Former professional cyclist and cycling team manager; admitted to doping during his career in 2007; resides in Denmark.
